summary: Researched on the evening of Wed 11 Nov for Thursday. 16 candidates (Nations League football, EuroLeague, ice hockey, ATP Stockholm, WTA Finals, CS2); 8 researched, 8 not reached because six games were already kept at medium confidence. Medium confidence: England over Croatia (Croatia effectively out of the group, England won the first meeting 7-0, but Konsa, Guehi, Saka, Palmer and others are out and Spain away follows on Sunday; p 0.77), Czechia v Spain (Spain already qualified and without Yamal, Oyarzabal, Rodri and Olmo, England next; p 0.80), Montenegro over Latvia (group leaders at home against a side with little to play for; p 0.765), Michelsen over Tabilo (fresher, better hard-court Elo, won their only meeting; p 0.74), Spirit over G2 (CS2 BLAST Rivals Bo3 on LAN, Spirit top 2 and 2-0 in the last meeting; p 0.73) and Gauff over Kostyuk (Kostyuk eliminated with a wrist problem; Gauff's own motivation is thin; p 0.68). Low confidence, never bet: Real Madrid v Crvena Zvezda (Campazzo, Maledon, Jantunen out; no lineups or rating). Excluded: Hurricanes v Kraken (NHL Global Series in Helsinki, neutral venue). Team news may change on match day, so the slip is rebuilt if the research is pushed again before its first game. No Stake or Rainbet prices were found; prices seen were DraftKings via ESPN for the football, Codere for Real Madrid, and tips.gg / footballpredictions listings for Montenegro.

checks.team_news: Spain (25-man squad for Prague per Flashscore/RFEF): Yamal (right knee, stays in Barcelona) and Oyarzabal (flu, recovering in San Sebastian) miss Prague and join after it for England; Barrenetxea injured and replaced by Jorge de Frutos; Rodri out (biceps femoris, about a month) and Dani Olmo out (adductor, back late November) per futboltotal; Eric Garcia not called. Back from injury: Porro, Nico Williams, Ferran Torres. Squad also has Pedri, Zubimendi, Merino, Fabian, Fermin, Cubarsi, Laporte, Huijsen, Cucurella, Grimaldo, Pino, Simon/Raya. Czechia (coach Santi Denia, in post since well before this week): all 24 called up fit per assistant Bejbl; Coufal and Hlozek had minor muscle issues but played at weekend (Hlozek 20 min, Coufal 90, Coufal tired); Sulc's ban was for the October game. I did not find De la Fuente's pre-match press conference text for Prague.
checks.lineups: No confirmed or credible predicted XI found for 12 Nov (searches for Sports Mole, Marca, AS, iSport pages returned only the October Oviedo match; no fresh XI from them). Context only: for the 3 Oct game in Oviedo De la Fuente made 9 changes vs the Croatia game (El Gol Digital/Comuniate) and still won 3-1, so heavy rotation is plausible again. Expected Spain core without Yamal, Oyarzabal, Rodri, Olmo is still Simon/Raya; Cubarsi, Laporte, Cucurella; Zubimendi, Pedri, Merino; N. Williams, Ferran, Pino/Fermin. Czechia expected to start Kovar, Coufal, Hlozek, Soucek-type regulars; unverified.
checks.rotation: Spain played Croatia 29 Sep and Czechia 3 Oct in October, then 12 Nov at Letna (Prague), then England at the Metropolitano on Sun 15 Nov (decisive for top spot: Spain 12 pts, England 9). Spain already qualified for the quarter-finals (El Gol Digital/Marca-type reports), so De la Fuente may rest players for England, though Yamal and Oyarzabal are being kept for Sunday. This is not a confirmed heavy rotation (no official XI yet), so no hard exclusion. Czechia: Prague on Thu, Osijek vs Croatia Sun 15 Nov.
checks.motivation: Group A3 after 4 games: Spain 12 (4W), England 9, Croatia 3, Czechia 0. Spain already through to the QF, lower stakes before England. Czechia are bottom, 3 pts behind Croatia, and are fighting to avoid relegation to League B (second-weakest of the fourth-placed teams, one goal better than Turkey on goal difference), so they are highly motivated and at home.
checks.form: Spain: 4 wins from 4 in this Nations League (3-2 v England at Wembley, 2-1 v Croatia, 3-1 v Czechia, plus one more win), WWWWWW in all comps per Sports Mole before October. Czechia: lost all 4 (0-3 v England at home with Sulc sent off, 1-3 v Spain, lost to Croatia), DLLLL per ESPN; WLDLLL in all comps; Denia's side leaks goals but scored in games vs Spain (Slama).
checks.h2h: 3 Oct 2026 Spain 3-1 Czechia (Oviedo, Spain rotated 9 players). 2022-23 Nations League: Czechia 2-2 Spain in Prague and Spain 2-0 in Malaga. Czechia are rarely level with Spain recently; Spain win comfortably, but the 2-2 in Prague shows a draw is possible when Spain rotate.
checks.odds: ESPN/DraftKings close: Spain -525, draw +550, Czechia +1000; de-vigged about Spain 0.774, draw 0.142, Czechia 0.084 (DK is lower than Polymarket's 0.8164 for Spain). DK totals line 3.5 (over +110, under -140, about 0.55 under de-vigged), spread Spain -1.5 at -170 (about 0.60), Czechia +1.5 at +120 (opened +2.5 at -190, closed +1.5). Polymarket Spain win 0.815 flat over 24h (0.815 at both ends of the 1d price history, no move); draw 0.115, Czechia 0.065.
checks.models: ClubElo and eloratings.net could not be retrieved (clubelo API returned nothing, eloratings.net serves a JS reload page), so no bookmaker-free rating was read. Proxy only: DraftKings de-vigged Spain about 0.77 vs Polymarket 0.8164; Sports Mole's October preview predicted Spain 3-0 and Squawka also 3-0, but those are tips, not ratings.
checks.venue_weather: Generali Arena (Letna), Prague, Czechia's home ground (ESPN lists Generali Arena), 20:45 local, 19:45 UTC kick-off; a normal home venue, not neutral. No weather or pitch reports found; no extreme-weather signal.

games.reason: Fixture verified (Czechia v Spain, Nations League A3, Thu 12 Nov, Letna Prague, ESPN and ceskenoviny). No hard exclusion: no confirmed rotation, no coach change in the last 7 days (Denia is in post), not a derby. Spain are far better but come without Yamal, Oyarzabal, Rodri and Olmo, already qualified, with England on Sunday, so I trim Spain from the market 0.816 to 0.80 and give Czechia and the draw a little more. Draw about 12.5%, under the 25% ceiling for a straight win, so Spain to win is allowed.
games.main_risk: Rotation and low stakes for qualified Spain (9 changes v Czechia in October, England on Sunday, four key players out) leading to a draw or an upset by a motivated Czechia fighting relegation at home; the Czech side also scored in the October game. Fair price for Spain win 1.22 is thin versus the DraftKings de-vigged 0.774 (about 1.29).

checks.team_news: Tuchel's press conference (Brit Brief, 11 Nov): Ezri Konsa (knee knock) and Djed Spence (fitness) are both out, 'we will not take the risk'. The Hard Tackle (11 Nov) lists England absentees Rico Lewis, Chalobah, O'Reilly, Palmer, Mainoo, Rashford, Livramento (knee), Alex Scott (thigh), Saka (hamstring), plus Guehi (hip) withdrawn and Konsa out; James Hill called up for the first time. Croatia: Perisic suspended (red card vs Spain, per Karlobag/SoccerNews snippets). Pulled out or missing: Sutalo (hamstring), Pongracic (thigh), Jakic (foot), Kramaric (knee), F. Ivanovic (head), Juranovic, Erlic, Moro, Stojkovic. Modric is in the squad, listed with no injury, and is in the predicted XI. A Brit Brief headline about a 'clean bill of health' predates the Konsa/Guehi news.
checks.lineups: Only one predicted XI read (The Hard Tackle, 4-2-3-1). England: Pickford; Alexander-Arnold, Quansah, Branthwaite, Hall; Anderson, Rice; Rogers, Bellingham, Gordon; Kane. Croatia: Livakovic; Stanisic, Vuskovic, Caleta-Car, Gvardiol; Modric, Kovacic; Vlasic, Pasalic, Baturina; Budimir. No second source found. Croatian press (Index.hr, Sportske novosti) and Sports Mole searches returned only older matches, and the Sports Mole page for this game returned 404. No official XI yet.
checks.rotation: England: Thursday at home, then Spain away on Sunday 15 Nov (Metropolitano, Madrid), so some rotation risk. Nothing confirmed, and the England side is already thin through injuries. Croatia played Spain and Czechia in the previous window and face Czechia on Sunday. The flight is short for Croatia. No 5+ changes announced, so no hard exclusion.
checks.motivation: League A Group 3 after matchday 4 (fubo table, Fanatik): Spain 12 pts, England 9, Croatia 3, Czechia 0. England host Croatia on 12 Nov. Remaining games are Czechia v Spain on 12 Nov, then Croatia v Czechia and Spain v England on 15 Nov. Croatia can reach at most 9 points, so a win or draw likely seals England's quarter-final place (Brit Brief says England want to top the group). Croatia are effectively out and need a big win. The Spain game on Sunday decides the group win, which could lead Tuchel to manage minutes. The game still matters for England.
checks.form: England DWWLW (3-0-1 in the group, GD +3 per fubo): lost 3-2 to Spain, beat Czechia 2-0, beat Croatia 7-0 in Rijeka; lost only 2 of their last 14 (The Hard Tackle). Croatia DLLWL (1-0-3, GD -10): beat Czechia 2-1, then lost three straight including 0-7 to England and a 2-1 home loss to Spain; lost 7 of their last 11. No xG found.
checks.h2h: 13 meetings: England 8 wins, 2 draws, 3 defeats (The Hard Tackle). The most recent meeting was England 7-0 in Rijeka (Oct 2026), and earlier meetings include England 2-1 at Wembley in 2018. Croatia have lost heavily in this group, which points to few draws. The 7-0 score shows how high-scoring this matchup can be.
checks.odds: ESPN/DraftKings (scoreboard API, 12 Nov): England -425, draw +475, Croatia +900. De-vigged this is about 0.747 / 0.161 / 0.092, so slightly less England-heavy than Polymarket 0.794 / 0.133 / 0.074. DraftKings total 3.5: over +115, under -145 (de-vigged under about 0.56, in line with Polymarket 0.555-0.565). DraftKings England -1.5 -155 (de-vigged about 0.60 with Croatia +1.5 at +110). Polymarket England-win token (24h history): 0.775 at the start, 0.785 mid, 0.795 now, a drift up of about 2 points with no price shock. Squawka and Sporting Life previews pick England 3-0 and 3-1.
checks.models: eloratings.net could not be read (the fetch returned only an empty page shell), so no Elo figure is cited. Bookmaker-free proxies only: group goal difference (England +3, Croatia -10), the 7-0 result in the first meeting, and Croatia's 7 defeats in 11 games. This check is weaker than normal, which is why confidence is medium.
checks.venue_weather: Wembley Stadium, London (ESPN confirms the venue), Group A3, kick-off 19:45 UTC on Thursday 12 Nov. A normal home venue. No weather or pitch alert was found, but I did not check a forecast.

games.reason: England are clear favourites at home against a Croatia side beaten 7-0 in the first meeting and long out of contention. The draw chance at the market is 13%, well below the 25% limit for a straight win. DraftKings is less bullish on England (de-vigged about 0.75) than Polymarket, so I trimmed England to 0.77 and lifted the draw to 0.15. England are already short of many regulars and may rest or manage minutes with Spain away on Sunday. England win at 1.26 is the cleanest leg. Goals legs: both totals (over 2.5 at 1.50, under 4.5 at 1.33) look sensible given Croatia's defensive record, but the 7-0 first meeting shows how wide the goal range is, and England's attack is thin with Saka, Palmer, Rashford and Mainoo out. England -1.5 at 1.74 needs two goals and is more exposed to a rotated, injury-hit side.
games.main_risk: Draw or a tight England win: Tuchel has many injuries and Spain on Sunday, so rotation or a flat performance is possible, and Croatia (Modric, Gvardiol, Vlasic) can still hold a low-scoring game. Only one predicted XI was available, and the Elo rating could not be checked.

checks.team_news: Per footballpredictions.com (read today): Stefan Loncar is suspended; Adam Marusic is back in contention; Aleksa Maras could make his international debut. No other Montenegro injuries found. A Sports Mole preview from the earlier round listed Aleksa Latkovic as suspended for that game, not this one. No Latvia squad or injury list for this match was found in English or Latvian press (LFF, LSM and Delfi were not indexed). Latvia coach Paolo Nicolato has run short of senior players before. Jānis Ikaunieks, Roberts Uldriķis, Renārs Varslavāns, Vladislavs Gutkovskis, Alvis Jaunzems and captain Kristers Tobers were out for a Baltic Cup camp, and their status for this match is unknown.
checks.lineups: No confirmed or well-sourced predicted XIs for 12 Nov. Last Montenegro XI predicted by Sports Mole (vs Armenia): Popovic; Vesovic, Rubezic, Vujacic, Radunovic; Loncar, Jankovic, Adzic; Osmajic, Krstovic, Jovetic. Loncar is now suspended, so a change is needed in midfield. Starting11 shows Latvia's usual shape as 5-4-1 (Matrevics in goal, Ciganiks, Cernomordijs and Cirkins in the back five). Tips.gg expects Montenegro in a 4-4-2 under Mirko Vucinic. Confirmed XIs are not out until about an hour before kickoff.
checks.rotation: Montenegro play at home. The Armenia preview said Vucinic may rotate, and the 3-2 win over Armenia was the previous game. Latvia host Armenia on 15 Nov, and the trip to Podgorica is an away game for them. Both sides have had regular international-window rest. No heavy-rotation report for Montenegro, so the hard rule is not triggered.
checks.motivation: Per footballpredictions.com, Montenegro lead League C Group 2 with 10 points from four games and are chasing promotion to League B. Latvia are fourth with 1 point and 'have little to play for' (same source). Montenegro have the stronger incentive. A raw-points check: Sports Mole says Montenegro won 2-1 at Cyprus, 3-2 vs Armenia and 2-1 at Latvia.
checks.form: Montenegro: 2-1 vs Cyprus, 3-2 vs Armenia, 2-1 at Latvia (Vasilije Adzic scored twice in Riga, in minutes 3 and 56; Strods replied in minute 82). They are unbeaten in five matches and lost once in their last seven (Sports Mole). They have not kept a clean sheet recently, conceding in each of the three Nations League wins I could verify. Latvia: lost 0-2 at Armenia, lost 1-2 at home to Montenegro, and have lost three of their last five away games with 0.6 goals per away game (footballpredictions.com). Their one point comes from another fixture.
checks.h2h: Reverse fixture 2 Oct 2026: Latvia 1-2 Montenegro in Riga (Novosti, Sports Mole). Footballpredictions.com lists 75% of the last four meetings as over 1.5 goals and 75% as BTTS. A draw is not common in this pairing in the sources read. Montenegro are the clearly better side but have been conceding, which supports lower confidence on BTTS no.
checks.odds: Tips.gg: Montenegro 1.34, draw 4.98, Latvia 9.50. Footballpredictions.ai: 1.33 / 4.60 / 8.50. Kickoff.co.uk: Montenegro 1/3 (72%), Latvia 7/1. De-vigged these give Montenegro about 0.73-0.75, draw about 0.19-0.20, Latvia about 0.08-0.10, close to Polymarket de-vigged 0.7565 / 0.1671 / 0.0764. Footballpredictions.com: under 3.5 goals 4/11 (74%), Montenegro draw no bet 1/12. Polymarket 24h move on the Montenegro win token: 0.745 to 0.755 (+1 point, no concern). Polymarket Latvia 0.075, draw 0.165.
checks.models: Elo page (eloratings.net) would not render for my fetcher, so I have no Elo figures to quote. Model-style sources read: Footballpredictions.com predicts Montenegro 2-1 (tips: home win, over 1.5, BTTS); Footballpredictions.ai predicts a 2-1 Montenegro win; Kickoff.co.uk gives Montenegro a 72% win probability. Models agree on Montenegro as clear favourites, with a 2-1 modal score.
checks.venue_weather: Stadion Pod Goricom / Gradski Stadion, Podgorica (home ground, normal venue), kickoff 19:45 GMT (20:45 CET). No weather or pitch problem reported in the sources read; I did not find a forecast, so conditions are unverified.

games.reason: Montenegro are group leaders at home against a fourth-placed Latvia side with little to play for, and they won the reverse fixture 2-1 away. Polymarket and the bookmaker prices I saw agree closely (home about 0.73-0.76), so I keep p near the market with a small upward lean for home motivation and Latvia's weak away scoring. The draw is estimated at 16%, under the 25% limit for a straight win. Goals views: both teams have scored in their meetings, Montenegro have conceded in every recent game, and Latvia score little away, so BTTS no is slightly less likely than the market says. Over 1.5 and under 3.5 are supported by the 2-1 modal scores.
games.main_risk: A draw or narrow result against a deep-defending 5-4-1 Latvia. Montenegro midfielder Stefan Loncar is suspended, XIs are unconfirmed, and Montenegro have conceded in every recent game, so BTTS is a real chance. I could not find Latvia squad news or Elo ratings, so confidence stays medium.

checks.team_news: No injury or withdrawal reports found for either player in searches on 11 Nov. Both are in the draw and both won on the ATP Stockholm results page. Michelsen beat Hanfmann 6-2 6-3 (R1) and J.M. Cerundolo 6-3 6-2 (R16, Tue 10 Nov, completed per ATP and Mykhel). Tabilo (4th seed, R1 bye) beat qualifier Sonego 7-6(2) 6-7(7) 7-5 on Wed 11 Nov on Center Court. Nothing announced about injury, but he played a long three-set match, so fatigue is a risk. Not confirmed: any physical issue for either player.
checks.lineups: Order of play for Thu 12 Nov not published on the ATP pages I could read (daily schedule only showed Day 5). Not confirmed: court and time. The candidate file has the start at 12:00 UTC. The round is most likely the quarter-final: Michelsen and Tabilo have both won their R16 matches. I did not see the official bracket.
checks.rotation: Michelsen: straight sets twice, about 1h08 in R1 and a short R16, so he is fresh. Tabilo: 3 sets with two tiebreaks (7-6, 6-7, 7-5) on Wed, then back on Thu with one day of rest, a clear fatigue edge to Michelsen. Same venue, no travel for either.
checks.motivation: ATP 250 quarter-final, a place in the semi-final, ranking points and prize money at the end of the season. Both are playing in the last tournament of the ATP week (8-14 Nov). No sign of either having less to play for.
checks.form: Michelsen: won both Stockholm matches in straight sets, 4 sets lost 5 games in R1 and 5 games in R16 (6-2 6-3, 6-3 6-2). Tabilo: needed three sets and 2 tiebreaks to get past Sonego (qualifier). Results from before Stockholm were not checked.
checks.h2h: One meeting: Miami Open R3, hard court, 23 Mar 2026, Michelsen won in three sets (stringtension shows the score as 3-6 6-3 6-4 in compressed form; reading inferred). Michelsen leads 1-0. Tabilo is a left-hander.
checks.odds: No bookmaker price found besides Polymarket. Searches returned only March 2026 Miami odds (Stats Insider Michelsen about 58%, Tabilo $2.37, Michelsen $1.57). I did not get a de-vigged price for the Stockholm match, nor the 24h Polymarket move. Market p is Michelsen 0.75, Tabilo 0.25 per candidates file. This is a gap in the checks.
checks.models: Tennis Abstract Elo (list updated 2026-11-09): Michelsen Elo 1879.9 (rank 25), hard Elo 1851.6 (rank 19). Tabilo Elo 1782.2 (rank 59), hard Elo 1731.8 (rank 57). The hard-Elo gap of 120 points implies about 67% for Michelsen, below the 75% market. The fatigue edge and the h2h partly support the market.
checks.venue_weather: Kungliga Tennishallen, Stockholm: indoor hard court, no weather impact, same venue for both players all week.

games.reason: Fixture verified: Bybit Stockholm Open (ATP 250), Michelsen (6th seed) v Tabilo (4th seed), both through R16 on 10 and 11 Nov. Michelsen is the better player on hard-court Elo (about 120 hElo points), is fresher after two straight-set wins, and leads the h2h 1-0. Tabilo played 3 sets with 2 tiebreaks the day before. Elo implies about 67%, below the market 75%, so p is set at 0.74, one point under the market. Confidence medium, not high, because the order of play is unconfirmed and no second price source was found.
games.main_risk: Tabilo is a left-hander with a big serve and a tight match is decided in a few points; indoor 250 matches can turn on a tiebreak. Elo says Michelsen should be nearer 67% than 75%. Missing facts: Thursday order of play and a non-Polymarket price.

checks.team_news: No injuries, illness or stand-ins reported for either side in any source read today. tips.gg preview (9 Nov) lists Spirit as magixx, zont1x, donk, sh1ro, tN1R (coach hally) and G2 as huNter-, HeavyGod, matys, NertZ, r1nkle (coach sAw), with no stand-ins listed. Strafe notes only that FUT signed SunPayus. HLTV and the team socials were not reachable, so this rests on preview articles.
checks.lineups: Predicted fives only, from one preview source (tips.gg), with nothing official found: Spirit magixx/zont1x/donk/sh1ro/tN1R; G2 huNter-/HeavyGod/matys/NertZ/r1nkle. Both teams played their groups' opening matches on 11 Nov with these names per the listing, and no change was reported.
checks.rotation: Group B opening matches were Spirit 2-1 FUT (11 Nov, ~06:30) and G2 2-1 MOUZ (11 Nov, ~09:36) per esportnow.gg, both Bo3. The 12 Nov Spirit-G2 Bo3 at 09:30 is the winners' match of a double-elimination group (both teams 1-0), so the loser still gets an elimination game. Spirit played a full three-map match yesterday, so there is some fatigue risk, but G2 also went three maps and both sit on the same LAN schedule. Spirit won BLAST Open Porto in late Aug 2026.
checks.motivation: Winners' match of the four-team double-elimination Group B. The top 3 of 4 advance, and the group winner goes straight to the semifinals while #2 and #3 start in the quarterfinals. Both teams are already close to qualifying, so the stake is the semifinal bye, and neither side is under elimination pressure.
checks.form: Spirit: won BLAST Open Porto (Aug 2026, beat MOUZ 3-1 in the final), HLTV top 2 in late October per tips.gg, and beat FUT 2-1 on 11 Nov (dropped a map). G2: beat MOUZ 2-1 on 11 Nov but went 0-3 at PGL Masters Bucharest recently per tips.gg, and the article calls their group draw unfavorable. Outright odds on Melbet: Spirit 5.00, G2 34.00.
checks.h2h: Last meeting: Spirit beat G2 2-0 in the BLAST Open Porto 2026 upper-bracket semifinal (Fragster, Aug 2026). A scores24 preview for that Porto match noted that in three of the last four meetings Spirit closed out G2 without needing a third map. Earlier 2024-25 meetings were mixed per profilerr, with G2 taking some, so the series is not one-sided.
checks.odds: Polymarket match winner Spirit 0.735 / G2 0.265, flat over the last 24h (price history 0.735 throughout, no move). Polymarket map markets: Map 1 Spirit 0.645, Map 2 Spirit 0.715, Spirit -1.5 maps 0.445, over 2.5 maps 0.415. Melbet outright odds on tips.gg (9 Nov) show a big gap, Spirit 5.00 to win and 2.75 to reach the final versus G2 34.00 and 19.00. I found no direct bookmaker price for this match (no HLTV odds page), so there is no de-vigged second price.
checks.models: No HLTV ranking page was readable. tips.gg says Spirit were in HLTV's top five in mid-October and top two in late October, and that invites were based on VRS Global (Oct 2026). G2 are well below Spirit on both outright odds and form per the same article. No Elo-style model figure found.
checks.venue_weather: LAN at AsiaWorld-Expo, Hong Kong (BLAST Rivals Fall 2026, 11-15 Nov), a standard tier-1 event venue. Group stage is all Bo3. This is not a Bo1, not neutral-unusual, and indoors, so weather is irrelevant.

games.reason: Verified tier-1 BLAST Rivals Fall 2026 Group B Bo3 on LAN (esportnow.gg schedule, Polymarket title confirms Bo3), so not a Bo1 and eligible for the slip. Spirit are the stronger side by ranking, recent title, and a 2-0 win in Aug 2026, which supports the 0.735 market. I keep p at 0.73 because CS2 Bo3 variance is high and Spirit needed three maps yesterday. Rated medium rather than high because no HLTV match page, official lineup confirmation or second bookmaker price was available.
games.main_risk: CS2 Bo3 variance: G2 are a capable upset team (they have beaten Spirit before, mixed 2024-25 results) and just beat MOUZ 2-1. Spirit dropped a map to FUT yesterday, so fatigue or a map-pool veto loss on G2's best maps could cost a map or the series. The winners' match gives G2 a safety net, so Spirit may not be at full intensity, and lineups were not officially confirmed.

games.reason: Hard rule: neutral/unusual venue. This is an NHL Global Series regular-season game played at Veikkaus Arena in Helsinki, Finland, not in Carolina (Thu 12 Nov 2026, 12:00 PM ET = 17:00 UTC, 7:00 PM Helsinki local; Kraken are the nominal home team). Hurricanes and Kraken play two games in Helsinki (Nov 12 and Nov 14). Fixture and date verified via Live Nation Finland, TickPick and the Hurricanes site listing; a single SportBusy page listing Seattle's Climate Pledge Arena conflicts with all other sources and is treated as an error. The Polymarket 'home' label (Hurricanes) therefore carries no home-ice edge.
games.main_risk: Neutral European venue with travel/jet lag and no true home advantage; market home price 0.715 is for a nominal 'home' team not playing at home.

checks.team_news: Real Madrid (coach Pedro Martinez) without Facundo Campazzo (left hamstring, out indefinitely, Eurohoops/Sportando 3 Nov), Theo Maledon and Mikael Jantunen (hurt vs Fenerbahce), long-term Gaby Deck and Usman Garuba; Max-Sport/Infobae 11 Nov also list Chuma Okeke as absent while Infobae says Okeke is back in the squad (sources conflict); Nick Smith Jr. cleared from a foot injury; debutant Pablo Mera in the squad. Zvezda (coach Ibon Navarro) travelled to Madrid without centre Christian Koloko because of visa problems, expected to be resolved by Thursday morning (Eurohoops 11 Nov 18:15); no other Zvezda injuries found. The euroleaguebasketball.net injury report returned HTTP 429 and was not used.
checks.lineups: No predicted or confirmed starting fives found in 2 searches (Infobae preview, Eurohoops, Max-Sport 403). Madrid has no Campazzo or Maledon at guard; Koloko's availability for Zvezda is unresolved.
checks.rotation: Madrid: lost Round 10 at home to Panathinaikos 115-112 in OT on Wed 4 Nov, then beat UCAM Murcia 90-71 on Sun 8 Nov (Liga Endesa); about 3-4 days rest, no back-to-back. Next games at Olimpia Milan then Barcelona. Zvezda: won 62-57 at Olympiacos on Fri 6 Nov, 5 days rest, travelling to Madrid. This is a single game week for both, so there is no double-round fatigue.
checks.motivation: Regular season Round 11. Zvezda are 2nd at 7-3; Madrid are 8th at 6-4 after a 6-game winning streak ended vs Panathinaikos. Both need wins for top-4 home court; no rotation or tanking motive.
checks.form: Madrid: 6-game EuroLeague win streak, then OT home loss to Panathinaikos; best offence in the league at 97.8 ppg, depleted backcourt. Zvezda: 7-3, best defence in the league at about 74 ppg allowed, won 103-73 vs Bayern (29 Oct) and 62-57 at Olympiacos (6 Nov).
checks.h2h: 2025-26: Zvezda won 90-75 in Belgrade (17 Oct 2025); Madrid won 95-72 in Madrid; Madrid won 103-82 at Movistar Arena on 16 Apr 2026. Style clash: Madrid's top offence against Zvezda's top defence.
checks.odds: Codere preview: Real Madrid 1.37 / Zvezda 3.05, handicap Madrid -6.5 at 1.85, total 173.5; de-vigged Madrid about 0.69, which matches Polymarket 0.695. No Polymarket 24h move was fetched, so none is claimed. No Stake or Rainbet price seen.

checks.motivation: After Tuesday: Noskova 2-0 and already through, Gauff 1-1, Pegula 1-1, Kostyuk 0-2 and eliminated (thesportsencounter, tennis365). Gauff can only advance if she beats Kostyuk AND Pegula loses to Noskova (tennis365). Gauff said 'the goal is just to win the next match' and that she 'wouldn't be too upset' if she won and still missed out. Kostyuk has nothing to play for except pride and said she wants to fight for every point. Soft risk: Gauff's edge on motivation is smaller than it looks, and she is not out of it if Pegula's result goes her way.
checks.form: Gauff: beat Pegula in three sets on Sunday, then lost 3-6 3-6 to Noskova, who broke her five times and won 18 of 24 points on Gauff's second serve (serve was the main problem). Gauff beat Kostyuk 6-2 6-2 in the Cincinnati QF in Aug 2026. Kostyuk: 0-2 here, both in straight sets (6-2 6-4, 6-2 7-5), with a wrist problem and little match play. Kostyuk beat Pegula twice earlier in 2026 (Brisbane, Madrid) but lost to her here.

games.reason: Fixture verified from three pages (Mykhel, StringTension, WTA/ESPN reports) and no withdrawal or walkover announced. Gauff is the clear favourite on every model I read (Elo 62-72%), leads h2h 4-2 (4-1 on hard) including 6-2 6-2 in August, and Kostyuk is eliminated, 0-2 with straight-set losses, a wrist problem and little match play. I moved the market by -0.5 points for Gauff (0.685 to 0.68) and sit slightly below it because the evidence is mixed, not clearly in either direction.
games.main_risk: Gauff just lost 3-6 3-6 to Noskova with her serve breaking down, and her own motivation is thin: she can only advance if she wins and Pegula loses to Noskova, and she said she would not be too upset to miss out. A loose, low-intensity dead-rubber style match against an unburdened Kostyuk, who has beaten Gauff in 2 of their 6 meetings (incl. Doha 2025), is the most likely way the leg fails. No bookmaker price was found, so the market price rests on Polymarket alone. The two Tuesday results above were confirmed from multiple outlets, but no pre-match news since then was found.
